question: GQ-001
subject: the two rules that decide what enters the corpus could not be tested
the_gap: age-settled (which decides the RIGHTS BASIS a book is admitted on) and the correspondence filter (which decides whether an item is a book at all) both lived inside build-want-list.mjs, a script that fetches from the Internet Archive at import time. Neither could be asserted without a network round-trip.
why_it_matters: these are the highest-consequence rules in the repo, and "cannot be pointed at a fixture" is the defect class that has cost the most here — it had reached the rights layer
the_fix: lib/selection-rules.mjs, imported by both build-want-list and build-external-passages. One definition, so the two call sites cannot drift.
the_refactor_is_behaviour_preserving: 39 cases compared between the old inline implementations and the extracted ones — 8 years x 4 grades plus 7 titles — with ZERO disagreements
a_false_alarm_i_had_to_resolve: rebuilding the want-list showed 1802 -> 1840 items and 261 grade changes. That is IA returning a different result set on a fresh query, not a logic change — proven by comparing the two implementations on FIXED inputs instead.

the_probe.boundaries_not_happy_paths: 1928 upgrades and 1929 does not; a missing year never upgrades; none and not-a-designation are never promoted however old the work

i_reintroduced_a_defect_and_caught_it: my first placement put the probe ABOVE the probe_done helper, so it ran and its result was silently dropped — the suite still read 23, not 24. That is exactly the decorative-probe defect I fixed yesterday, reproduced within a day.
